stem: After an RN delegates an appropriate task to unlicensed assistive personnel, which action best demonstrates appropriate supervision?

options.A: Assume responsibility ends once the task is assigned
options.B: Monitor performance, evaluate the outcome, and provide needed follow-up or feedback
options.C: Automatically redo every delegated task regardless of how it was performed
options.D: Transfer responsibility for supervising the task to another unlicensed assistive staff member

rationale: NCSBN's delegation framework describes delegation as a process in which licensed nurses and delegatees have defined responsibilities and the delegating nurse oversees the process. Appropriate delegation includes supervision, evaluation, and follow-up rather than ending responsibility at the moment of assignment. Nurses must also follow the laws and rules of their jurisdiction.
educational_objective: Recognize that safe delegation requires ongoing supervision and evaluation of the delegated activity and its outcome.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Delegation; National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation
source_version_date: Current NCSBN delegation page; joint guidelines effective 2019-04-29
source_locator: Delegation Model; responsibilities of delegating nurse and delegatee / National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation
source_claim_supported: Delegation is an ongoing process with defined responsibilities for the delegating nurse and delegatee; the licensed nurse oversees the process and must practice within jurisdiction-specific delegation laws and rules.
correction_summary: Removed the conversational cueing and retained the core NCSBN delegation principle of supervision/evaluation after assignment. Avoided overstating a universal state-law rule because delegation authority varies by jurisdiction.
audit_findings: B is the only option consistent with an ongoing supervised delegation process. A abandons oversight; C is unnecessary if delegation is safely completed; D improperly transfers licensed-nurse oversight to UAP. No second answer remains.
